title: Joe Robichaux band, Lunsford and the war
summary: After Desvigne he joined Robichaux, recalls its record personnel, the band became Lunsford, broke up when the draft took members, then Freddie Coleman.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: See, were you on any of those records that Joe Robichaud made? I forget now.
Well I know he had a small outfit then. I forget that you were all known. Yeah, I know. I was quite a large man. There was Gene Porter, Gishard, Ransom Nolens, Eugene Ware, Bucket, and then Joe.
They were on the other record.
You see Bucket, who's he? What did he play? Drums. The drums.
He's in Chicago now. Yeah. He was from Chicago. I don't know his name. All I know is Bucket. I wasn't familiar with that either.
It was funny. And after Joe Robichaud, do you remember?
Oh yeah, we converted Joe Robichaud band into John Lunsford.
And after we had to disband because we had too many young fellas. Knuckle Sam.
And the war came along then, huh? Yeah.
Knuckle Sam took him. And then we started on the Freddie Coleman band.
And after that, I'm freelancing. Yeah.
